title: Degree-zero localization on an ambient affine open
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $L$ an invertible module [def-sc-invertible-module], $s\in\Gamma(X,L)$ and $F$ a quasi-coherent module [pqf-def-coherent]. Let $S\subseteq X$ be an open with underlying set the nonvanishing locus $X_s$ [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module], and let $U\subseteq X$ be affine open. For $p\geq0$, write $A_p(W)=H^p(W,F)$ for open module cohomology [def-sc-open-module-cohomology] and $Q_p(U)$ for the additive fraction presentation [def-sc-cohomology-fraction-presentation], whose generator $[n,\xi]$ has $\xi\in H^p(U,F\otimes L^{\otimes n})$ and whose relations are $[n,\xi]=[n+b,s^b\xi]$. For $p=0$, There is an additive isomorphism $e_p:Q_p(U)\longrightarrow A_p(U\cap S)$ such that, for every $n\geq0$ and every numerator $\xi$, multiplication of $e_p([n,\xi])$ by $s^n$ is the restriction of $\xi$ from $U$ to $U\cap S$. Multiplication here is induced on cohomology by the module morphism $F\cong F\otimes\mathcal O_X\xrightarrow{1\otimes s^n}F\otimes L^{\otimes n}$.

source.place: Tags 09MR (degree-zero and affine-open paragraphs), 01PW, and 01E1 (2); consulted at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09MR, /01PW and /01E1

proof.text: Restrict L, F and s to the affine scheme Y=U.toScheme. Mathlib restrictFunctor, restrictFunctorIsoPullback and restrictAppIso identify sections and tensor powers naturally. Invertibility follows from pullback and restriction preserves quasi-coherence. Apply affine_section_localization on Y, and identify its nonvanishing open with the preimage of S using the stalk criterion.

The left exact sections functor has the natural comparison Functor.rightDerivedZeroIsoSelf. Its naturality in coefficient morphisms and the derived restriction natural transformation identify degree-zero cohomology and all transition maps with ordinary sections on U and U cap S. Take the direct sum over numerator degrees. The additive closure of section fraction relations is their module span as an additive subgroup: scalar multiplication sends the generator (n,b,t) to (n,b,r*t), so the additive closure is a submodule and contains the span; the reverse inclusion is immediate. Consequently the direct-sum equivalence descends to the section fraction quotient and preserves every generator.

Compose the quotient equivalence with the affine section localization equivalence and the inverse degree-zero comparison on the target. The sections map of the tensor morphism is tmulSection with s^n. Naturality and the formula in affine_section_localization therefore give exactly the required equation for every numerator. Empty U and zero s require no separate nonzero or inhabited hypotheses.
